title: Tensor base change of a compatible spectrum model
statement: Let $d:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $X_0,Y_0$ schemes over $S$, and $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ an $S$-morphism. Define $X_T,Y_T,f_T$ by base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $V\subset Y_0$, $W\subset S$ be opens, $V_T=p_Y^{-1}(V)$, $U_T=f_T^{-1}(V_T)$ and $W_T=d^{-1}(W)$. Let $R,B,C$ be commutative rings with maps $a_B:R\to B$, $a_C:R\to C$ and an $R$-algebra map $\varphi:B\to C$. Suppose given $e_0:W_T\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, $q:V_T\to W_T$ with $q\circ\iota_{W_T}=p_T\circ\iota_{V_T}$, $e_B:V_T\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $e_C:U_T\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}(a_B)\circ e_B=e_0\circ q$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)\circ e_C=e_B\circ(f_T|_{V_T})$. Then for every $t:L\to T$, commutative $R$-algebra $A$, and $e:t^{-1}(W_T)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ satisfying $e_0\circ(t|_{W_T})=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to A)\circ e$, the base change of $f_0$ along $t\circ d$, restricted to the inverse image of $V$ under its target first projection, is isomorphic as an arrow to $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes_R\varphi)$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. No finite-type or limit hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Let Y_T=Y₀×_S T and X_T=X₀×_S T. Write V_T=p_Y⁻¹(V) and U_T=f_T⁻¹(V_T). The equation for q factors the target chart through W_T=d⁻¹(W); the restricted f_T factors the source chart through the same open. For t:L→T, paste the original pullback squares and open restriction squares to identify the target chart over L with V_T×_{W_T}t⁻¹(W_T) and the source with U_T×_{W_T}t⁻¹(W_T). Both identifications commute with the chart map.

Transport the fibre products along e0,eB,eC and e. The target compatibility hB identifies its structure map with Spec(aB); source compatibility follows from hφ and φ commuting with R. Apply pullbackSpecIso R A B and pullbackSpecIso R A C to identify target and source with Spec(A tensor_R B) and Spec(A tensor_R C). The map is Spec(id tensor φ), because its composites with the A and B projections are the prescribed identity and φ maps. Pullback uniqueness proves equality, giving the arrow isomorphism. This includes zero rings.
